entries.why: market_profile.py measured, across five timeframes on gold and across nine markets at H1, that hours differ enormously in two ways. Cost per unit of movement spans 3.1% to 175.6% depending on hour and timeframe, and the variance ratio spans 0.44 to 2.21 - some hours extend their moves, others give them back. Those are estimates, not selections: every hour is reported and none was chosen for looking good, and the instrument's own tuning log shows the estimates moving 0.00% and 0.05% when knobs that cannot change the measured quantity were varied. Separately, rigorous_search.py has now closed the question of whether a price SHAPE predicts direction here: 0 of 21,889 rules beat a simulated null, and the top 60 lost money at zero cost on 0 of 9 markets. What remains untested is a different claim - that the market's measured STRUCTURE tells you which of two ordinary entries to reach for.
entries.change: Take the hour classification straight off the instrument with no freedom to adjust it: hours with variance ratio >= 1.10 are 'extending', <= 0.90 are 'reverting', and hours costing more than 1.5x the median cost per unit of movement are refused outright as a cost decision. Then run two deliberately ordinary entries through run_e01 - a Donchian-20 close breakout and a 1.5-ATR fade - in the MATCHED arrangement (breakout in extending hours, fade in reverting hours) and in the SWAPPED arrangement (breakout in reverting hours, fade in extending hours). The control is the swap rather than a blind run, because a blind control would differ in trade count as well as in matching, and the matching is the only thing under test. Report the matched-minus-swapped difference per market and pooled across markets.
entries.criterion: One comparison: matched minus swapped, pooled across the nine markets, positive with an across-market |t| clearing the ledger floor. A difference near zero says the regime split is real as a description and empty as a guide - which is a specific falsifiable thing to learn about the instrument and is NOT the same as the map being wrong.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026. The hour classification is computed by the instrument on each market's own history; the entries are fixed in source before the run and neither their parameters nor the VR and cost thresholds are swept.

result.note: REJECTED, and in the direction the instrument's own diagnosis predicts. Matching momentum entries to hours measured as extending and reversion entries to hours measured as reverting came out -0.0172R WORSE than the swapped control, across-market t -1.77, positive on 3 of 9 markets. Per market: XAUUSD -0.0088, XAGUSD -0.0513, EURUSD -0.0093, GBPUSD -0.0277, USDJPY +0.0255, AUDUSD +0.0130, USDCHF -0.0493, USDCAD -0.0511, NZDUSD +0.0043. No single market's difference clears |t| 1.25. WHY IT IS NEGATIVE RATHER THAN ZERO, established from measurements alone. vr_is_illiquidity.py found the variance ratio correlates +0.42/+0.41/+0.41/+0.53 with cost per unit of movement at M1/M5/M15/H1 and runs INVERSELY to movement: the six highest-VR hours on gold H1 cost 1.4x more and move 1.5x less than the six lowest. In a thin book price drifts rather than standing still because nobody is on the other side to push back, and a run of small one-way moves is exactly what a high variance ratio measures - so raw VR cannot separate a trend from an empty book. Matching therefore sent breakouts into the dead expensive end of the day. The size checks out: the cost gap between high-VR and low-VR hours is about 6.3% of range, roughly 0.06R, which is LARGER than the -0.0172R observed. So the cost differential alone more than accounts for the result and there is no need to claim the regime information is anti-predictive - if anything a small positive information content is partly offsetting the cost penalty, though that is not separable at this resolution. TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING. The map is not refuted: cost per unit of movement spanning 3.1% to 175.6% across hour and timeframe, and the VR-cost correlation itself, are measurements that stand. What is refuted is using RAW VR to choose entries. And on the signal-count question: matched produced 310 signals per market per year, about 2,800 across nine markets, four times the 700/year target. Signal scarcity was never the constraint - each signal loses 0.11R to 0.24R, and producing more of them loses money faster, not slower.

entries.why: The arithmetic of this entire project fits in three numbers. The largest drift-adjusted skill ever measured here is +0.073R, at zero cost. The cost map just measured says H1 charges a median 12.5% of an hour's own range and H4's cheapest hours charge 3.1%. At H1 no measured edge survives; at H4's cheap end a +0.073R gross skill would net around +0.04R. That is the only configuration in 828 hypotheses where the arithmetic is not already lost before the entry rule is chosen, and it comes from the instrument rather than from a search. The regime-matching test just failed at -0.0172R, and its failure was traced to cost rather than to direction - high-variance-ratio hours are the expensive dead ones - which points at the same place.
entries.change: Take the two ordinary entries already fixed in profile_setups.py - a Donchian-20 close breakout and a 1.5-ATR fade, neither re-tuned - and run them on H4 bars restricted to the hours the instrument measures as costing no more than 1.5x the median cost per unit of movement. Refusing the expensive hours is a cost decision and free; the hypothesis is only whether the resulting book is non-negative. Compare against the identical entries on the identical H4 bars with NO hour restriction, so the difference isolates the cost constraint rather than the timeframe change. Report per market and pooled across nine markets, at real bid/ask through run_e01.
entries.criterion: Pooled expectancy at real bid/ask NON-NEGATIVE on the cost-restricted H4 book, with the restricted book beating the unrestricted one by at least the declared margin and an across-market |t| clearing the ledger floor. A restricted book that is still negative says the cost map is correct about which hours are dear and that the edge is too small to survive even the cheapest of them - which closes the timeframe question rather than leaving it open.
entries.test_period: Nine markets, H4 resampled from the H1 cache, 2004-2026. The hour classification is computed by the instrument on each market's own history. Neither entry parameter nor the 1.5x cost threshold is swept.

result.note: REJECTED, and it closes the timeframe question as the criterion said it would. Restricted book -0.1639R, unrestricted -0.1723R, so the cost constraint is worth +0.0084R at t +1.78 - real, consistent in direction, and nowhere near enough. Positive on 0 of 9 markets. 256 signals per market per year restricted. A DESIGN FLAW IN MY OWN TEST, found mid-run and recorded rather than quietly fixed: H4 bars start only at 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 UTC, so the 24-hour map has six populated cells there and the 1.5x cost cutoff removes exactly one of them (20:00, at 13.51% against a 6.0% median). A constraint that drops one slot in six is barely a constraint, so the per-market differences are mostly sampling noise. I should have checked the cell count before applying a 24-hour map to a six-slot timeframe. THE NUMBER THAT SURVIVES THE FLAW, because it does not depend on the restriction: both H4 arms are as negative as H1's, despite the map measuring H4 at 6.0% of range against H1's 12.5%. The cost saving is cancelled by a gross edge that degrades at the longer horizon - the same conclusion tsmom_d1.py reached at D1 by a different mechanism. AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFRAMES ALL OF IT. Running both entries at ZERO cost: momentum -0.0436/-0.0593/-0.0427 at H1 and -0.0175/-0.0558/-0.0492 at H4 on gold/EURUSD/GBPUSD; reversion -0.1221/-0.1217/-0.1129 at H1 and -0.1520/-0.1490/-0.1368 at H4. Every gross expectancy is NEGATIVE. I have repeatedly written in this ledger that the edges here are smaller than the costs. That is wrong. These entries lose money before a single spread is charged, and cost is a penalty stacked on an already-negative base rather than the reason for it. The practical consequence is that the whole cost-reduction avenue - cheaper venue, longer timeframe, affordable hours - cannot help, because zero cost still loses. Reversion is consistently the worse of the two by about 0.09R, which says moves at these horizons continue more than they revert; that is a real directional fact and is NOT a licence to flip the rule, since a bracketed trade's expectancy does not negate when its direction does.

entries.why: bracket_bias.py measured, on random timing at zero cost with an independently written engine that reproduces run_e01 exactly, that this project's standard bracket loses 0.09R to 0.12R per trade before any entry is chosen: -0.0931 on gold, -0.1175 on EURUSD, -0.1090 on GBPUSD. That is larger than the entry skill this repo has ever measured (+0.039 to +0.062R) and larger than its costs (0.011 to 0.073R), and it is present in all 828 prior hypotheses. The cause is the stop width: widening it from 1x to 2x cuts the penalty to -0.0315, a 70% reduction consistent in direction on every market. The martingale guard could never have caught this - a constant-volatility fixture cannot detect a volatility-clustering effect.
entries.change: Re-run the same two ordinary entries - Donchian-20 close breakout and 1.5-ATR fade, neither re-tuned - through the identical engine with stop_mult 2.0 instead of 1.0, at REAL bid/ask, on nine markets H1. Compare against the same entries at stop_mult 1.0 on the same bars, and against matched random timing at both widths so the bracket penalty and the entry skill are reported separately rather than summed. Note in advance that doubling the stop doubles the R denominator, so skill and cost both shrink by roughly half in R terms; the question is whether the penalty falls faster than the skill does.
entries.criterion: Pooled expectancy at real bid/ask NON-NEGATIVE with the 2x stop, and the improvement over the 1x stop clearing the declared margin with an across-market |t| above the ledger floor. A book that improves substantially but stays negative says the bracket was a real and large defect AND that fixing it is still not sufficient - which is a different and more useful finding than either 'it works' or 'nothing changed'.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 at real bid/ask. The 2x stop was selected from the random-timing control table alone, which never sees the real entries; no entry parameter is swept.

result.note: THE REGISTERED CRITERION FAILS, EVEN THOUGH THIS FILE'S MECHANICS WILL PRINT ACCEPTED. The ledger checks margin and floor, and both are met by a wide margin: improvement +0.0706R against a declared 0.02, across-market t +9.97 against a floor of 4.72, positive on 18 of 18 market-entry pairs. But the criterion written to disk before the run has a third condition the mechanics do not check - pooled expectancy at real bid/ask NON-NEGATIVE - and that fails at -0.0719R with 0 of 18 books positive. Recorded as failing the criterion. THE THREE TERMS, POOLED. net expectancy -0.1425 -> -0.0719 (+0.0706); bracket on random timing -0.1918 -> -0.0806 (+0.1112); entry skill +0.0492 -> +0.0087 (-0.0405). WHAT THAT DECOMPOSITION SAYS, INCLUDING AGAINST ME. The bracket was a real and large defect: halving its penalty improved every one of 18 books. But the entry skill did not merely halve with the doubled R denominator, which is what pure scaling would do - it fell to 18% of its former value, about 35% of what scaling alone predicts. So the skill measured at the 1x stop was substantially an artefact of that tight stop rather than directional information that survives a wider one. This retracts my own reading from earlier in this session, where I reported the entries beating random timing by +0.039 to +0.062 and treated that as evidence the entries carry information. Those numbers were measured through the defective bracket and most of the advantage does not survive its repair. At a fairer bracket these entries have essentially no skill: +0.0087R. AND THE REPAIR IS INCOMPLETE. The bracket at 2x is still -0.0806 on random timing at zero cost, nowhere near zero. Widening the stop halves the penalty; it does not remove it. An R normalised by a per-trade stop distance appears to carry an intrinsic negative expectancy that stop width alone does not fix, and that remains unexplained.

entries.why: The instrument measured a volume-at-price structure that has never been turned into a setup: the value area holds 60% of the daily range, the next day touches the prior day's value area 93.8% of the time, and price closes inside its own value area 66.2% of the time. I reported the 93.8% as a near-tautology baseline - two overlapping daily ranges touch almost by construction - and then never tested anything against it. That is the one part of the original request, to read where volume sits and what each zone does, that produced a measurement and no test. Separately, the bracket work since then means this can be run on a corrected engine: at a 2x stop the random-timing control returns -0.005R once the measured 73.3% stop-first rate is applied, against -0.048R at 1x, so a difference of the size an edge might have is no longer swamped by the exit's own penalty.
entries.change: Compute the prior session's value area and point of control from the instrument's own volume-at-price routine, time-weighted where the volume column is unusable and volume-weighted where it is not, using only data from sessions that have closed. Then test the two opposing readings of that structure, both entered at the next bar's open through run_e01's mechanics at a 2.0x stop: ROTATION - price trades outside the prior value area and then closes back inside it, faded toward the point of control; BREAKOUT - price closes outside the prior value area having been inside it, taken in the direction of the break. Each against matched random timing with its own invalidation levels, nine markets H1, real bid/ask, with the three terms - net expectancy, bracket penalty, entry skill - reported separately rather than summed.
entries.criterion: Either reading, pooled across nine markets, showing drift-adjusted skill positive with an across-market |t| clearing the ledger floor AND net expectancy at real bid/ask non-negative. Both readings failing says the value-area structure is real as a description of where price spends its time and carries no directional information at this horizon - which is the same shape of answer the variance ratio gave, and would say the instrument's zone output is descriptive rather than predictive.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 at real bid/ask, 2.0x stop. Value areas are computed per session on closed data only; no zone parameter is swept and the 70% value-area definition is the instrument's existing one.

result.note: BOTH READINGS FAIL THE CRITERION, BUT NOT IN THE WAY THE CRITERION ANTICIPATED, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS. Rotation: net E -0.0670, bracket -0.0976, skill +0.0306, across-market t +2.52, skill positive on 7 of 9, expectancy positive on 0 of 9, 93 signals per market per year. Breakout: net E -0.0566, bracket -0.0772, skill +0.0206, t +2.28, skill positive on 8 of 9, expectancy positive on 1 of 9, 115 signals per market per year. Neither t clears the 4.72 floor and neither book is profitable, so the registered criterion fails on both of its conditions. WHERE THE CRITERION WAS WRONG. It said that both readings failing would mean the value-area structure carries no directional information. That is not what the numbers say: skill is positive on 7 of 9 and 8 of 9 markets respectively, which is not an absence of information. THE OBSERVATION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS, AND IT UNDERCUTS BOTH READINGS. These two setups are near-opposite - rotation fires on re-entry into the prior value area and fades toward the point of control, breakout fires on exit from it and follows the break - and BOTH show positive skill. If the value area carried directional information, one should win and the other should lose by a similar amount. Both winning says the measured skill is probably not directional at all but something the two share: each fires only when price is moving relative to the prior session's zone, while the random control enters at any time including dead ones. That would make the +0.03 a selection effect for being in the market when it moves, not a statement about which way it goes - which is exactly why it cannot pay the bracket penalty and the spread, since knowing that something will happen is not knowing its sign. That explanation is consistent with the data and UNTESTED; it is recorded as the reading to check next, not as a conclusion. On the standing signal-count target: these produce 837 and 1,035 signals a year across nine markets, either side of the 700 asked for, and both lose money.

entries.why: Every positive skill number in this session was measured against a control that randomises TIMING only. Two results now suggest that control is too weak. First, the ordinary momentum and reversion entries both beat it. Second, and more tellingly, the value-area rotation and breakout setups are near-opposite readings of the same structure - one fades re-entry toward the point of control, the other follows the break away - and BOTH beat it, on 7 of 9 and 8 of 9 markets. If the value area carried directional information one should win and the other lose by a similar amount. Both winning says the measured skill is probably not directional at all, but something the two share: each fires only when price is moving relative to a prior zone, while a timing-only control enters at any bar including dead ones. That would make every +0.02 to +0.05 skill figure in this session a selection effect for being in the market when it moves rather than a statement about which way.
entries.change: Replace the timing-only control with one matched on MOVEMENT. For each real signal record its own bar's true range over ATR, bin those into deciles, then draw the control's entries from bars in the same decile in the same proportions, so the control sits in equally active conditions and differs from the real rule only in direction and level. Run it against four setup families already measured - Donchian-20 momentum, 1.5-ATR fade, value-area rotation, value-area breakout - on nine markets H1 at the 2.0x stop, and report skill against BOTH controls side by side so the drop is visible per family rather than asserted.
entries.criterion: If the skill measured against the timing-only control largely survives the volatility-matched one, it is directional information and every prior skill figure stands. If it collapses toward zero across all four families, then the controls used throughout this session were too weak and those figures measured activity selection rather than direction - which would retract the skill readings in the regime-matched, wider-stop and value-area entries alike. A mixed result, surviving in some families and not others, identifies which measurements to keep.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026, real bid/ask, 2.0x stop - the same books already measured, re-run against a stronger control rather than on new data.

result.note: THE CONTROL USED THROUGHOUT THIS SESSION WAS TOO WEAK, AND 91% OF EVERY SKILL FIGURE IT PRODUCED WAS ACTIVITY SELECTION. Skill measured against a timing-only control versus against one matched on the signal bar's own true-range decile: momentum +0.0253 -> +0.0049 (20% retained, t +0.63, positive on 6 of 9); reversion -0.0079 -> -0.0186 (already negative, worse); value-area rotation +0.0306 -> +0.0005 (2% retained, t +0.08, 5 of 9); value-area breakout +0.0206 -> +0.0191 (93% retained, t +1.77, 7 of 9). Across all four families +0.0171 -> +0.0015, nine percent retained. WHAT THIS RETRACTS, INCLUDING THINGS I CALLED ENCOURAGING. The regime-matched entry skill, the +0.0492 skill in the wider-stop comparison, and the value-area rotation skill were all measured against timing-only controls and are mostly not directional information. A rule that fires only when something is happening beats a control that enters at any bar including dead ones, without knowing which way the something goes. The tell was already visible and I named it before running this: rotation and breakout are near-opposite readings of one structure and BOTH beat the timing control, which cannot happen if the structure carries direction. THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS SESSION. run_e01_control, used across this repo's 830 hypotheses, randomises timing with matched risk ratios - dist over ATR - which matches trade GEOMETRY but not the activity level of the bar the signal fired on. Every skill number in this project that leans on it inherits the same weakness. I am not restating those results here; I am recording that the instrument they used has a measured 91% inflation on the four families tested. WHAT PARTIALLY SURVIVES. Value-area breakout retains 93% of its skill at +0.0191 with t +1.77 on 7 of 9 markets. That is the only family where the effect looks directional rather than selectional, and it is still far below the 4.72 floor and still cannot pay the bracket penalty and the spread.

entries.why: Audit check 8 measured that random_like builds a control whose stop sits a third as far away as the rule's - dist/ATR median 0.559 against 1.638 - so R, which divides by that distance, is scaled differently in the two books. Every skill figure in bracket_bias, wider_stop, value_area_setups and vol_matched_control was read across that gap, and the vol_matched_control result that 91% of apparent skill was activity selection was itself measured through the defective control. Both the claim and its retraction rest on the same broken instrument, so neither currently stands. The four families have to be re-measured through a control that inherits the rule's geometry before anything about them can be said.
entries.change: Replace random_like with controls.py, which for each real signal records its own dist/ATR ratio, draws a donor bar from a matched stratum, and SYNTHESISES an invalidation level at that same ratio on the donor bar - so the two books have identical risk geometry by construction. Run all eight levels C0 through C7 on the four families momentum, reversion, value-area rotation and value-area breakout, across the nine-market H1 panel at real bid/ask with a 2.0x stop. The decision quantity is skill against C7 - structure-context matched with direction randomised - which is the only level that requires knowing which way rather than merely when.
entries.criterion: A family carries directional information only if its skill against C7 is positive with a cross-market t above the floor the cumulative hypothesis count implies, currently 4.72. Skill against C1 that does not survive to C7 is activity, session or regime selection and is reported as such with the level named. If no family clears C7, the finding is that these four families carry no directional information at this horizon once geometry, timing, activity, volatility, session, regime and range position are all held constant - and the earlier 91%-retraction figure is superseded by a number measured on a correct instrument rather than merely repeated.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026, real bid/ask, 2.0x stop - the same books, re-measured through a corrected control rather than on new data. No holdout is touched.

result.note: REJECTED. No family carries directional information at C7, and the strongest is reversion at t -0.14; all four are NEGATIVE against the strongest control. By family, skill against C7: momentum -0.0116 (t -1.28, positive on 2 of 9); reversion -0.0011 (t -0.14, 4 of 9); value-area rotation -0.0056 (t -0.95, 3 of 9); value-area breakout -0.0094 (t -1.17, 3 of 9). THE EARLIER NUMBERS WERE MOSTLY INSTRUMENT. vol_matched_control measured +0.0171 against a timing-only control. On the cleaned frame with a geometry-matched control the same quantity is +0.0026 to +0.0066, and at one family it is negative. Two defects account for the difference and both are now fixed: random_like took the random bar's own high or low as the invalidation level, so its stop sat a third as far from entry as the rule's while R divides by that distance; and 29% of every bar in the sample was a weekend or rollover hour the venue did not quote, which collapsed Wilder ATR to 6.5% of its Thursday level by Sunday and made the engine reject 84.8% of Monday bars against 56.9% of Thursday's. THE 91% ACTIVITY-SELECTION CLAIM IS SUPERSEDED, NOT CONFIRMED. A synthetic rule that selects busy bars and faces a coin shows no skill at any level once geometry is matched - |t| below 2 at all eight, C1 included. There was no activity artifact to remove; the 91% was the geometry gap. WHAT THE PROFILE SHOWS INSTEAD. Several levels are significantly NEGATIVE: momentum against session-matched -0.0095 t -2.79 on 1 of 9; reversion against C5 -0.0113 t -2.63; value-area rotation against regime-matched -0.0149 t -3.16 on 1 of 9; value-area breakout against C5 -0.0190 t -2.91 on 1 of 9. All four families do systematically WORSE than matched random entries. The mechanism is measured rather than guessed: R divides by a stop distance set from ATR, these rules fire on high-ATR bars, and a larger denominator earns a smaller R for the same price move. Under this normalisation selecting volatile moments is a cost. That makes R-through-a-bracket a poor instrument for asking whether directional information exists, which is the next thing to separate.

entries.why: Every one of the 837 hypotheses in this ledger has been scored as R through a stop-and-target bracket, and the control hierarchy has just measured that this instrument is not neutral about direction. R divides by a stop distance set from ATR; all four families fire on high-ATR bars; a larger denominator earns a smaller R for the same price move. The result is that all four families score NEGATIVE against matched controls, with intermediate levels reaching t -3.16, and the mechanism is a property of the measure rather than of the market. A measure that charges volatility selection cannot answer whether directional information exists, because it penalises the rules that select movement whether or not their direction is right. The question has been asked through the wrong instrument for 837 hypotheses.
entries.change: Measure direction with no bracket at all. For each signal at bar t, take the entry price as the mid open of t+1 and the exit as the mid close of t+h, for h in 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 and 48 bars, and report the signed forward move three ways: raw in price units, divided by the pre-signal ATR at t, and divided by the spread at t. No stop, no target, no G12 tie-break, no one-position-at-a-time rule - none of which exist in the question being asked. Compare against the same C0 to C7 controls, which supply only a bar and a direction here. Report sign accuracy alongside the mean, since a signal can be right about direction and wrong about magnitude or the reverse, and the bracket conflates them.
entries.criterion: Directional information exists in a family at a horizon if the signed forward move beats the C7 control - same activity, volatility, session, regime and range position, direction coined - with a cross-market t above the floor the cumulative count implies, currently 4.73, and the same sign on at least 6 of 9 markets. If the RAW and the ATR-normalised measures disagree in sign or significance, the difference is the volatility-selection term and is reported as such rather than resolved by preferring one. If nothing clears at any horizon in any family, the conclusion is that these representations carry no directional information at any horizon from one hour to two days, measured without any execution assumption at all - which is a far stronger statement than the bracket could support, and the remaining question becomes whether a different TARGET than direction is predictable.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame, mid prices for the move and real spread for the cost scaling. No holdout is touched.

result.note: REJECTED ON THE REGISTERED QUANTITY, WITH A LARGE SECONDARY RESULT THAT IS REGISTERED SEPARATELY. The registered decision quantity was the signed forward move over pre-signal ATR against C7. Best cell is reversion at h=1: +0.0043 ATR, t +1.89, positive on 7 of 9. Zero of 24 family-horizon cells clear the 4.74 floor. SIGN ACCURACY IS A DIFFERENT STORY AND THE CRITERION REQUIRED IT REPORTED. Sign skill against C7, in percentage points, cross-market t, markets positive: reversion h=1 +2.60pp t +16.76 on 9 of 9; reversion h=3 +2.27pp t +20.92 on 9 of 9; reversion h=6 +1.68pp t +9.50 on 9 of 9; momentum h=1 -3.46pp t -34.07 on 0 of 9; momentum h=3 -2.79pp t -17.57 on 0 of 9; value-area breakout h=1 -2.49pp t -11.30 on 0 of 9. Every family decays monotonically toward zero by h=48. THE CONSISTENCY CHECK THE VALUE-AREA TEST FAILED, THIS ONE PASSES. Fading is right and following is wrong by comparable magnitudes on every market, which is what a single mechanism looks like from two sides. The value-area rotation and breakout pair both beat a weak control, which is what an instrument artifact looks like. WHY THE SIGN EDGE DOES NOT BECOME AN EXPECTANCY. Reversion at h=1 wins the direction 52.24% of the time and the magnitude-weighted edge is +0.0043 ATR. A symmetric payoff at that win rate would be worth about 0.031 ATR. It is worth an eighth of that, so the wins are small and the losses are large - the signature of mean reversion, and the precise reason a high win rate has never produced a positive expectancy anywhere in this ledger. The spread is about 0.13 ATR on gold H1, so the edge is roughly 3% of one round trip. AMBIGUITY IN MY OWN CRITERION, RESOLVED CONSERVATIVELY. The registration said the decision quantity was the signed forward move and separately that sign accuracy must be reported. It did not say which one decides. I am treating the magnitude as the registered quantity because it is the economically meaningful one, recording REJECTED, and registering the sign effect as its own hypothesis with its own falsification tests rather than claiming a pass on the reading that flatters me.

entries.why: Measured without any execution assumption, the fade and the follow families disagree about direction in mirror image on every market in the panel. Reversion is right 52.24% of the time at one hour against a matched control's 49.64%, t +16.76, positive on 9 of 9; momentum is right 46.23% against 49.69%, t -34.07, negative on 9 of 9; value-area breakout -2.49pp on 0 of 9. Every family decays monotonically to zero by 48 hours. Two opposite readings of one structure landing on opposite sides by comparable amounts is what a single mechanism looks like, and it is the consistency check the value-area pair failed when both of them beat a weak control. But a t of 34 is not a plausible size for a market edge, and the magnitude-weighted version of the same measurement is only +0.0043 ATR at t +1.89, so the wins are small and the losses are large. Before this is called a finding it has to be established what it IS, and the leading candidates are not exotic: unconditional one-bar negative autocorrelation that any fade inherits and that the families add nothing to, or microstructure noise in the observed price that reverts by construction.
entries.change: Ask what the sign edge is made of, with five measurements that separate the candidates. One: the unconditional fade - go against the previous bar's own move on every bar - which establishes how much of the effect any fade inherits for free. Two: the conditional add - the reversion family's sign skill measured against that unconditional fade rather than against a random control. Three: the lag test - run the identical rule off bar t-1's close instead of bar t's, entering at the same t+1 open, which leaves genuine multi-bar reversion intact and removes anything that depends on the most recent quote. Four: the magnitude decomposition - mean win, mean loss, and the win rate that would be needed to break even, reported in spread units so the economic size is visible. Five: cross-period stability across 2004-2014 and 2015-2026.
entries.criterion: The effect is a genuine conditional signal only if the reversion family retains a positive sign skill against the UNCONDITIONAL FADE with a cross-market t above the floor, currently 4.74, and on at least 6 of 9 markets, AND survives the one-bar lag with at least half its magnitude. If it does not survive the lag, it is microstructure and is recorded as such. If it survives the lag but adds nothing over the unconditional fade, then the finding is a property of the price series and not of the representation, and the families are redundant descriptions of it - which is a real finding about the market and a negative one about 837 hypotheses of setup search. If the magnitude decomposition shows the required breakeven win rate exceeds the measured win rate, the effect is information that cannot be monetised at this horizon, and that is to be stated plainly rather than pursued.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame, mid prices, no bracket. No holdout is touched.

result.note: CONDITIONAL SIGNAL CONFIRMED AND ECONOMICALLY INFEASIBLE. Both mechanism clauses of the registered criterion are met and the economic clause fires. WHAT IS REAL. Fading the previous bar's own move, unconditionally, on every bar, wins the direction 51.71% of the time - t +17.84 against 50%, positive on 9 of 9 markets, across 2004-2026. The reversion representation adds +0.53pp on top of that free effect, t +5.96 against the 4.74 floor, positive on 9 of 9. It survives the one-bar lag test with 58% of its magnitude retained, so it is not purely microstructure, though 42% of it does live in the most recent quote. It is stable: 52.87% in 2004-2014 and 51.72% in 2015-2026, decaying but present in both halves. This is the first conditional directional signal this project has established, and it is established without any execution assumption at all - no stop, no target, no tie-break, no one-position rule. WHAT IT IS WORTH. Mean win 9.053 spreads, mean loss 9.706, payoff 0.933. The win rate needed to break even ignoring cost is 51.75% and the measured 52.24% clears it. The win rate needed while PAYING ONE ROUND TRIP is 59.91%, and 52.24% is short by 7.67 percentage points. Gross edge +0.1201 spreads per trade; net of the spread, -0.8799. The information is worth twelve percent of what it costs to act on it, and it would have to be roughly eight times larger to break even. FAILURE CODE: COST_DOMINATED. Not NO_DIRECTIONAL_SKILL - the skill is there, measured on 349,000 signals across nine markets, 9 of 9 positive on every test. THE UNITS MISMATCH IS MINE. I declared a minimum improvement of 0.02 at registration, which is an R figure, while the decision quantity of this hypothesis is a probability. The ledger reads the margin as not met and it is right to; the criterion text specifies a t above the floor on at least 6 of 9 markets and survival of the lag, and those are what this is judged on. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A REJECTION. 837 hypotheses failed without establishing whether anything was there. This one puts a number on it: there is directional information at the one-hour horizon, it is small, it is stable, and the distance between it and tradability is a factor of eight in the ratio of edge to spread. That ratio is now the research target - not a better rule.

entries.why: The one-hour reversal is real - 51.71% unconditional, 52.24% conditional, 9 of 9 markets, both halves of twenty-two years - and worth +0.1201 spreads per trade against a round trip that costs 1.0. The gap is a factor of eight and it is not a gap in the rule. It is a ratio between two quantities that scale differently: the spread is a property of the quote and is roughly constant in price terms whatever bar length is used to make a decision, while the size of a predictable move grows with the horizon over which it is predicted. If a reversal effect of similar relative strength exists on four-hour or daily bars, the same percentage edge is worth several times more spreads. If it does not - and the one-hour effect decayed to nothing by forty-eight hours when the SAME signal was simply held longer - then the information lives at a horizon whose costs it cannot pay, and that is a structural answer rather than a failed search.
entries.change: Resample every market's cleaned H1 bid and ask series to H2, H4, H8, D1 and W1 by taking the first open, the running high and low and the last close on each side, and for gold additionally build M5, M15 and M30 from the cached minute data. Run the same two rules at each - fade the previous bar unconditionally, and the reversion representation computed on that timeframe's own bars - and report the signed move from the next bar's mid open to that bar's mid close in SPREAD UNITS, where the spread is the real quote spread at the entry bar's open and therefore does not change with the bar length. Report alongside it the sign rate, the win rate needed to break even while paying one round trip, and the median spread over median true range for that timeframe.
entries.criterion: A timeframe is viable if the gross edge in spread units exceeds 1.0 - the round trip - with a cross-market t above the floor, currently 4.74, and the same sign on at least 6 of 9 markets. The ratio of edge to cost peaking below 1.0 at every timeframe would mean the reversal information is structurally unmonetisable at retail spreads regardless of representation, which is the strongest negative result this project could produce and would redirect the remaining work onto a different target than direction. A peak that rises with bar length without reaching 1.0 identifies how much cheaper execution would have to be, and that number is worth having even though it is not actionable here.
entries.test_period: Nine markets 2004-2026 resampled from the cleaned H1 frame, plus gold minute data 2019-2026 for the sub-hourly rows. No holdout is touched.

result.note: REJECTED, AND THE SHAPE OF THE REJECTION IS THE RESULT. Zero of ten timeframes clear the registered bar. THE SCALING LAW, PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN AND CONFIRMED. The docstring stated in advance that if the reversal were a constant fraction of each horizon's own volatility the edge in spread units would grow as the square root of bar length. Fitted over six timeframes with nine markets each, the exponent is +0.536. H1 +0.1552 spreads becomes W1 +2.2020, which is 14.2x over a 168x bar length where a square root predicts 13.0x. The effect is very slightly stronger at long horizons than pure volatility scaling, not weaker. Full table in spread units: M1 +0.0054, M5 +0.0189, M15 +0.0878, M30 -0.1062, H1 +0.1552 t +2.86 on 8 of 9, H2 +0.2194 t +2.42 on 8 of 9, H4 +0.1207, H8 +0.2383, D1 +0.5711 t +2.50 on 8 of 9, W1 +2.2020 t +0.82 on 6 of 9. The weekly point estimate is the only one above one round trip and it has no power behind it - roughly 1,071 bars a market and a cross-market t of 0.82. THE TERM THAT DECIDES IT SCALES DIFFERENTLY FROM THE EDGE. The spread is paid once per trade whatever the horizon, so measuring in spread units makes every longer hold look better. Financing is charged per night and is LINEAR in the horizon. Edge grows as T^0.536 and cost as 1 + 1.2616*T/24 using gold's known long swap of 534.9 points against a 424-point median spread. Two curves of those shapes cross once, so the net has a single maximum: it sits at T = 2.68 hours and is -0.878 spreads. There is no horizon at which this information pays, and its own best point is short by seven eighths of a round trip. THE QUESTION TURNED ROUND, BECAUSE ONLY ONE SIDE OF THE SWAP IS KNOWN. The spec gives gold's long swap; the short side is not in this repository and a rule that is short half the time may pay less. So: the financing rate at which this breaks even is 0.2038 spreads per night, or 86 gold points. The known long rate is 535 points. Financing would have to be 6.2 times cheaper. AND WITH NO FINANCING AT ALL. Interpolating the two measured long horizons rather than the whole fit, the gross edge reaches one round trip at about 54 hours - roughly 2.2 days. That is where this information would be worth acting on if carry were free, which is why the swap figure rather than the edge decides the whole question. FAILURE CODES: COST_DOMINATED and TIMEFRAME_INAPPROPRIATE. Not NO_DIRECTIONAL_SKILL at any point.

entries.why: The economics are now pinned down rather than guessed. The net of edge minus cost has a single maximum at 2.68 hours, where the cost is 1.105 spreads and the unconditional reversal delivers about 0.23. Every previous search in this project looked for a rule with a positive expectancy and had no idea how large an effect would have to be; this one has a number. It needs roughly five times the unconditional amplitude, or an equivalent reduction in the denominator, and there are only two ways to get either: find states where the predictable move is much larger than usual, or trade only where the spread is much smaller than usual. Gold's cheapest hour costs 6.3% of that hour's range against a 12.5% median and a 36.5% worst, so the second lever is worth about a factor of two on its own and is measurable before any search.
entries.change: A pilot of roughly 200 hypotheses organised as family, mechanism, variant and parameters rather than a flat list of rules. Seven families: conditioning the unconditional fade on each measured state variable at its extremes; two and three bar event sequences; multi-scale states where an H1 decision is conditioned on the H4 context; rare dislocations at 2, 3, 4 and 5 ATR; session and rollover boundaries; cross-market conditioning; and spread-percentile conditioning, which attacks the denominator instead of the numerator. Every hypothesis is scored as the signed move from the next bar's mid open to the mid close one, two and three hours later, divided by the real spread at the entry quote, against C1 and C7 controls, on all nine markets. Each is assigned failure codes from measured quantities. The objective of the pilot is to learn WHY hypotheses die and where amplitude concentrates, not to find a winner.
entries.criterion: A hypothesis is a research candidate only if its gross edge in spread units exceeds 1.105 - the measured cost at the 2.68-hour maximum - with a cross-market t above the floor the count implies and the same sign on at least 6 of 9 markets, and if it survives C7. Nothing short of that is called promising, whatever its significance, because an effect that is significant and smaller than its own cost is an information finding and this project already has one. If no hypothesis clears, the deliverable is the failure distribution over the eighteen codes and the measured shape of where amplitude concentrates, which decides what the expanded phase searches and what the measurement layer needs. The pilot explicitly does not touch the sealed holdout.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame, mid prices for the move and the real quote spread at entry for the cost. No holdout is touched.

result.note: NO RESEARCH CANDIDATE BY THE REGISTERED CRITERION, AND THE CLOSEST THING THIS PROJECT HAS PRODUCED. 127 hypotheses across eight families. Five exceed the 1.105-spread economic bar with a cross-market t above 3 on at least 6 of 9 markets, all of them one shape: fade a bar whose range exceeds k ATR when the bar before it was quieter than q ATR. Best cross-market t among them is +3.64 against a floor of 4.85. Not cleared, so no research candidate, so the sealed holdout is not opened. WHERE AMPLITUDE CONCENTRATES, WHICH IS THE PILOT'S REAL OUTPUT. Mean gross edge in spread units by family: AMPLITUDE +1.561 (best +4.001), CHEAP +0.259, STATE +0.231, and SEQUENCE, CLOCK, MULTISCALE and CROSS all at 0.000 mean with bests of +1.576, +0.421, +0.361 and +0.177. Cross-market conditioning on EURUSD's own move found nothing at all, so the information is in the instrument rather than in the dollar. Clock conditioning found nothing, so the effect is not a time-of-day phenomenon. The denominator lever worked exactly as the tradability layer predicted: conditioning on the cheapest decile of spread-over-ATR cut the median from 0.108 to 0.045 and raised the edge from an unconditional 0.23 to 0.578, a factor of 2.5 for free. WHAT THE SURVIVOR SURVIVED. Skill against the full hierarchy: C1 +1.342, C3 +1.741, C5 +1.363, C7 +0.972 with cross-market t +2.26 on 8 of 9 - the direction survives matching on activity, volatility, session, regime and range position. Parameter surface is a plateau with a gradient, neighbourhood mean 62% of peak and monotone in both axes. Cross-period +0.857 in 2004-2014 and +1.625 in 2015-2026, stronger in the recent half. Leave-one-market-out swings the t by 17%. Entry delayed one bar retains 75%. Jaccard overlap with the second candidate 0.000, so they are distinct bets. THE FALSIFICATION THAT MATTERED MOST. Removing unquoted bars earlier in this session means two bars adjacent in the frame need not be adjacent in time, so a quiet bar before the rollover followed by a gap-containing bar would match this rule perfectly and would survive every control in the hierarchy, none of which matches on the clock skipping. Requiring the quiet bar, the entry bar and the whole three-hour exit window to be exactly hourly retains 95% of the edge on 95% of the signals. It is not a calendar artifact. THE STATISTIC WAS CHANGED AND THE CHANGE IS DECLARED. A cross-market t on nine market means has eight degrees of freedom and cannot exceed about 3 even for an effect present and identical everywhere, so judging it against a floor calibrated for many-observation trial statistics asks for power it structurally does not have. The replacement is a bootstrap resampling calendar months with all nine markets moving together, preserving serial correlation inside a month and cross-market correlation across them. It gives n 17,144 over 272 months, edge +1.316, SE 0.359, t +3.67, 95% interval [+0.627, +2.022], and 71.7% of draws above the cost. Both statistics are reported everywhere. Neither clears 4.85. FAILURE CODE: BELOW_MULTIPLICITY_FLOOR, a code added because this candidate returned UNKNOWN_FAILURE and UNKNOWN is supposed to mean the taxonomy has a gap. It fails nothing named. More searching cannot fix it, because the floor rises with every hypothesis spent looking; only independent data can.

entries.why: The expand-after-quiet candidate survives every structural test - the full control hierarchy to C7, a parameter plateau with a monotone gradient, both halves of twenty-two years, leave-one-market-out, a delayed entry, and the contiguity check that would have exposed it as a rollover-gap artifact - and its point estimate of +1.316 spreads exceeds the 1.105 cost. It is held back solely by a bootstrap t of 3.67 against a floor of 4.84 that 1,085 hypotheses have earned. More searching on the same nine markets cannot resolve that, because the floor rises with every hypothesis spent. Only data that was never part of the discovery can. The engineering audit recorded that USDSEK sits in the cache with a full 2003-2026 series and has never been used by any hypothesis in this repository; it carries a USD leg so it is not part of the sealed holdout either. It is one market and cannot establish the effect, but it can falsify it, and it costs nothing to ask.
entries.change: Run the candidate on USDSEK at the parameters frozen from the nine-market panel - fade a bar whose true range exceeds 1.5 ATR when the previous bar was under 0.7 ATR, entry at the next mid open, exit at the mid close three hours later, scored in units of the real spread at the entry quote - together with the unconditional previous-bar fade as a calibration, and the C7 control. The parameter surface is computed as well but only as description; the decision rests on the frozen point, which was fixed before this market was loaded.
entries.criterion: The candidate is falsified on fresh data if its edge on USDSEK is negative or below the unconditional fade measured on the same market. It is consistent with the panel if the edge is positive, exceeds the unconditional fade, and lies within the panel bootstrap's 95% interval of [+0.627, +2.022]. One market cannot confirm anything - a single positive result here does NOT make this a finalist and does NOT license opening the sealed holdout - but a negative one would end the line, and that asymmetry is the whole reason to run it.
entries.test_period: USDSEK H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame. Never used by any hypothesis in this repository. The sealed holdout is not touched.

result.note: FALSIFIED ON FRESH DATA, AND THE FLOOR CALLED IT FIRST. On USDSEK - a full 2003-2026 series in the cache that no hypothesis in this repository has ever used, and which carries a USD leg so it is not part of the sealed holdout - the frozen candidate returns +0.093 spreads on 1,661 signals, a month-block bootstrap t of +0.34, a 95% interval of [-0.442, +0.654] that contains zero, and a skill against the C7 control of -0.004. It does not beat the unconditional fade on the same market, which is the criterion's falsification clause, and it falls far outside the panel's [+0.627, +2.022]. THE GRADIENT DOES NOT REPRODUCE EITHER, AND THAT IS THE MORE TELLING HALF. On the panel the edge rose monotonically as the preceding bar got quieter - column means falling across all four steps from 0.5 to 0.9. On USDSEK 2 of 4 steps fall and the column means are U-shaped: 0.5 +0.401, 0.6 +0.276, 0.7 +0.078, 0.8 +0.120, 0.9 +0.277. A gradient is much harder for noise to imitate than a level, which is why it was declared as the thing to watch before this market was loaded, and it is absent. WHAT DID REPRODUCE. The unconditional previous-bar fade returns +0.115 spreads on USDSEK with a bootstrap t of +4.56 and a 95% interval of [+0.067, +0.164], against +0.155 on the panel. The universal effect is present on the fresh market at comparable size. The conditional one is not. So this is not a failure of the data or of the measurement - the instrument found what it was supposed to find and did not find what was not there. THE DISCIPLINE LAYER WORKED EXACTLY AS DESIGNED. The candidate was the best of 1,085 hypotheses at a bootstrap t of 3.67 against a floor of 4.84, which is the expected maximum of that many trials at the measured trial dispersion. A statistic below the expected maximum of pure noise IS what noise looks like, the ledger refused to promote it, the sealed holdout was not opened, and independent data agrees. ONE MARKET CANNOT SETTLE THIS ALONE and the asymmetry was stated before the run: a positive result would not have promoted the candidate, a negative one ends the line. It is negative. FAILURE CODE: CROSS_MARKET_INSTABILITY, replacing BELOW_MULTIPLICITY_FLOOR. The sealed holdout remains examined: false.

entries.why: The economic model that killed every horizon assumed financing accrues continuously, at swap times T over 24. It does not. Swap is charged at one moment - the daily rollover - so a position opened and closed inside the same session pays exactly zero of it, and this repository's own cost rules already require forcing a close thirty minutes before rollover and forbid holding through it. That changes the shape of the problem completely: without the linear financing term there is no single maximum at 2.68 hours, and the only cap on the horizon is the length of the session itself. Working in points rather than spread units, the reversal is worth about 65.8 points at one hour and grows as T to the 0.536, so it reaches the live account's quoted 260-point gold spread at about thirteen hours - which is inside a single session. The extrapolation is close enough to breakeven to be worth measuring directly rather than trusted, and the direction of the error is unknown.
entries.change: Search the intraday window directly instead of extrapolating. For each entry hour from 0 to 19 UTC and each hold length in 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 hours, where the exit falls at or before 20:00 UTC and inside the same trading day, form the signal from the market's own move over the PREVIOUS L hours - matching the scaling law's construction, in which a longer horizon means a longer bar rather than a stale one-hour signal held longer - and fade it. Score the signed move from the entry hour's mid open to the exit hour's mid close, in points and in units of the real spread at the entry quote, with the cost being one round trip and no financing whatsoever. Report the whole surface over entry hour and hold length, and run the C7 control on the best cells.
entries.criterion: A cell is viable only if its gross edge exceeds one round trip with a month-block bootstrap t above the floor the cumulative count implies and the same sign on at least 6 of 9 markets, and if its skill against C7 is positive. The surface as a whole is the deliverable either way: if the best cell falls short, the amount by which it does - measured rather than extrapolated - is the final statement on whether this information is reachable at retail cost, because eliminating financing is the last lever the economics leaves and there is nothing behind it. A cell that clears on the panel is NOT a finalist until it also reproduces on USDSEK, which has already falsified one candidate that passed every structural test on the panel.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame, plus USDSEK held back as the fresh-market check. No holdout is touched.

result.note: REJECTED, AND IT CLOSES THE ECONOMIC QUESTION. Zero of 64 cells clear the registered bar. Best cell: enter 07:00 UTC, hold 3 hours, exit before the rollover so no financing is paid at all - gross edge +0.717 of one round trip, cross-market t +2.70 on 8 of 9, month-block bootstrap t +4.14, skill against C7 +0.714 at t +3.18 on 8 of 9, 5,221 signals a market. The shortfall is 0.283 spreads per trade and it is measured rather than extrapolated. Only 5% of bootstrap draws put it above cost. THE SCALING LAW DOES NOT SURVIVE INSIDE A SESSION. Mean edge by hold length: 2h +0.144, 3h +0.049, 4h -0.050, 6h -0.121, 8h -0.225, with mean points per trade going from +4.4 at two hours to -49.1 at eight. Longer is WORSE inside a day, the opposite of the cross-timeframe result, because a cross-timeframe bar spans sessions and an intraday window does not. The extrapolation that motivated this file predicted breakeven at thirteen hours; measuring it rather than trusting it was the right call. A MEASUREMENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, WHICH RESTATES EVERY EDGE FIGURE IN THIS RUN. Edge was being computed as the MEAN OF move/spread RATIOS. That is what a trader earns only by sizing inversely to each trade's own spread - putting the most capital exactly where the quote is thinnest - and it lets a handful of unusually tight quotes dominate. The economics is the RATIO OF MEANS, total move over total spread, because net per trade is mean(move) minus mean(spread). The gap is 1.3x on the unconditional H1 fade, 2.3x on gold's best intraday cell and 2.3x on USDJPY's. Restated: the unconditional H1 fade is +0.1198 rather than +0.1552, still positive on 9 of 9 at t +4.94; the cross-timeframe scaling exponent is +0.233 rather than +0.536, so H1 to W1 is 3.7x over a 168x bar length where a square root would give 13x; and the best intraday cell is +0.717 rather than +0.864. A SECOND UNIT ERROR CAUGHT AND NOT PUBLISHED. Pooling move and spread across markets adds gold points to pip points and produced a meaningless +0.109. The correct aggregation is per-market ratio of means then an equal weight across markets. WHERE THAT LEAVES THE ECONOMICS. At +0.233 the edge would not reach one round trip until roughly 8,900 hours, which is a year, and financing over a year is not a rounding error. Intraday, the best window reaches 72% of a round trip. Financing was the last lever - the spread cannot be negotiated, the horizon is capped by the session, and the floor rises faster than any search improves the best result. FAILURE CODES: COST_DOMINATED and TIMEFRAME_INAPPROPRIATE.

entries.why: On the corrected ratio-of-means metric zero of 127 pilot hypotheses clear the 1.105-spread bar with a t above 3 on at least 6 of 9 markets, where five appeared to on the inflated mean-of-ratios. Two shapes remain interesting and neither clears both conditions: stacking the cheap-quote filter on the amplitude condition gives the largest edges this project has produced - expand-quiet-cheap at 1.5 ATR reaches +2.631 of a round trip with a net of +1.526 - but only reaches t +1.99 on 345 signals a market; and tightening the amplitude condition to 1.2 ATR after a bar under 0.4 gives t +4.92 on 9 of 9, which clears the 4.84 floor, at an edge of +1.100 against a bar of 1.105, which is breakeven to within half a percent. As the condition tightens the edge rises and the sample falls, and the product never clears both. USDSEK has already falsified the plain version of this shape. Testing the remaining ones on it as a single batch rather than one at a time is what keeps this from becoming a sequential search of the only unexamined market this project has.
entries.change: Take the eight highest-edge pilot hypotheses, at parameters frozen from the nine-market panel, and run all of them on USDSEK in one pass: the three cheap-stacked amplitude variants, the four tightest amplitude variants, and the exhaustion-follow sequence. Score each on the ratio of means with the real spread at the entry quote, alongside the unconditional fade on the same market as calibration, and report every one of the eight rather than the best.
entries.criterion: A candidate is consistent with the panel only if its USDSEK edge is positive, exceeds the unconditional fade on that market, and exceeds one round trip. Reporting all eight is the point: if the panel effect is real the set should tilt positive, and if it is selection the set should scatter around the unconditional fade. A single positive among eight is what noise produces and will not be called a survivor. Nothing here can make a finalist or license opening the sealed holdout, which stays examined false regardless of the outcome.
entries.test_period: USDSEK H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame. The sealed holdout is not touched.

result.note: SCATTERED. The whole discovery phase collapses on the one market that had no part in producing it. All eight taken at once, at parameters frozen from the nine-market panel, panel edge against USDSEK edge in units of one round trip: expand-quiet-cheap/1.5 +2.631 -> -0.087; expand-quiet-cheap/1.2 +2.212 -> -0.234; expand-quiet-cheap/1.8 could not form a book; expand-after-quiet/1.5-0.4 +1.574 -> +0.363; expand-after-quiet/1.2-0.4 +1.100 -> +0.205; expand-after-quiet/1.8-0.6 +0.934 -> +0.289; expand-after-quiet/2.2-0.6 +0.924 -> +0.207; exhaustion/follow +0.751 -> -0.143. Mean across the set +0.086 against a panel mean of +1.447, a collapse of seventeen times. Four of seven beat the unconditional fade of +0.075 on the same market, which is what a coin gives. None exceeds one round trip; the best reaches +0.363, less than half. THE DESIGN IS WHY THIS IS READABLE. Running all eight in one pass and reporting every row was registered before the data was loaded, precisely so that a single positive among eight could not be promoted. Four of seven above the unconditional fade is the null, not a signal. THE PATTERN ACROSS THREE INDEPENDENT CHECKS IS NOW CONSISTENT. The floor of 4.84 said the panel's best candidate at a bootstrap t of 3.67 was what noise looks like at 1,085 hypotheses. The single-candidate USDSEK test agreed. This batch agrees. And the corrected ratio-of-means metric had already removed all five apparent clears from the pilot before any of that. Four independent lines, and none of them needed the sealed holdout. WHAT SURVIVES ALL OF IT. Only the unconditional previous-bar fade, which reproduces on USDSEK at +0.075 of a round trip on 126,392 signals, having reproduced on the panel at +0.1198 with a t of +4.94 on 9 of 9. It is real, it is universal, and it is worth between seven and twelve percent of what it costs to act on. FAILURE CODE: CROSS_MARKET_INSTABILITY for the set. The sealed holdout remains examined: false and has never been opened.

entries.why: Direction at a fixed horizon has now been measured to exhaustion and it fails for a structural reason: the payoff is the expected MOVE, which is small, while the cost is the spread, which is fixed. Every conditioning state tried raises the move by less than the factor needed, and the best of them collapsed on a market that had no part in producing it. But a bracket does not pay the expected move. It pays its own WIDTH. Entering with a symmetric bracket at plus or minus D and asking only which side is touched first, the expectancy is (2p-1)*D minus one spread, and D is a choice. At a bracket of 1.5 ATR with the spread near 12% of ATR, D is about twelve spreads, so breakeven sits at p near 0.54 rather than at a move five times larger than anything measured. A four point lift in which side is touched first would pay where a four point lift in sign accuracy does not. That is a different target with different economics and this project has never asked it directly. A third target, whether the next range is large, is non-directional and has the economics of a straddle; the pilot's only family carrying anything was the one conditioning on range states, which is a reason to ask it rather than a result.
entries.change: An expanded search over roughly 400 hypotheses evaluating every state against three targets rather than one. DIRECTION is the signed move over the spread, as before. PATH is the probability that a symmetric bracket at k ATR is touched on the signal's side first, at k in 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0, reported as the lift over the same bracket on matched control entries and converted to expectancy as (2p-1)*D minus one spread. EXPANSION is the next window's true range over the spread, non-directional, against the cost of straddling it. The out-of-sample split is built into the funnel rather than bolted on afterwards: every hypothesis is fitted on 2004-2016 and reported on 2017-2026, both periods printed for all of them, and only what passes both is taken to USDSEK.
entries.criterion: A hypothesis is promoted only if its expectancy exceeds one round trip in BOTH periods with the same sign on at least 6 of 9 markets in each, and its skill against C7 is positive in both. Reporting both periods for every hypothesis regardless is the point, because a set that is strong in the first period and scattered in the second is the signature this run has already seen twice. If no hypothesis passes both periods, the conclusion is that none of the three targets is reachable at retail cost on this data, which given that path asymmetry has a breakeven near 54% rather than a five-fold amplitude requirement would be the strongest negative this project can produce. Nothing here can open the sealed holdout.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1, discovery 2004-2016 and validation 2017-2026, with USDSEK held back behind both. No holdout is touched.

result.note: REJECTED ON ALL THREE TARGETS, AND THE THIRD ONE FAILED FOR A REASON WORTH MORE THAN THE OTHER TWO. 118 hypotheses, five targets each, fitted on 2004-2016 and reported on 2017-2026 with both periods printed for every row. DIRECTION: 63 of 118 positive in both periods but only 2 clear one round trip in both, and both are the shapes USDSEK already falsified. PATH ASYMMETRY: 0 of 118 at every bracket width. The arithmetic that motivated this target is sound - a symmetric bracket pays (2p-1)*D minus a spread, and at 1.5 ATR the bracket is 27 spreads wide so breakeven sits at p = 52.89% rather than at a five-fold amplitude increase - but the unconditional p is 50.08% and nothing lifted it. The closest was exhaustion-follow at +2.012 then +2.281 round trips, which failed the market-consistency requirement at 5 of 9 in the first period. EXPANSION, AND THE ERROR IN MY OWN FIRST VERSION OF IT. The first implementation scored the next window's true range over the spread minus two and returned numbers like +73 round trips. A range is not a profit: the whipsaw case where both sides trigger and neither runs has exactly the same range as the clean case. Rewritten as an actual breakout straddle - stops half an ATR either side of the open, take whichever triggers first, hold to the window close, less one round trip - it read +2.498 for a 2-ATR dislocation state against an unconditional -0.140, with a lift over the C7 matched control of +1.078 at t +4.94 on 8 of 9 markets. THAT NUMBER WAS A SCORING ASSUMPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. It counted windows touching both barriers inside one bar as no trade. Those are 19.9% of the candidate state's windows against 7.9% of an unconditioned bar, because the state is selected for volatility and volatility is what makes a bar span both levels. Scored as entered and stopped instead, the same state reads -0.647 and the lift falls to +0.113 at t +0.86. The gap between the two bounds is three round trips per armed window, larger than every other effect in this project combined, and neither bound was a measurement. GOLD MINUTE DATA RESOLVED IT AND IT RESOLVES AGAINST THE STRATEGY. For every ambiguous H1 bar from 2019 to 2026 the minute path says which barrier came first and what followed: 130 of 130 resolved windows in the dislocation state were stopped out, 53 of 53 in the cheap-dislocation state, 3,121 of 3,121 in the baseline. One hundred percent, none profitable, mean -16.2 to -25.8 spreads each, which is the -2X-minus-a-spread the geometry implies. The resolved figures land on the pessimistic bound: -0.259 against -0.244, +1.464 against +1.494, -0.950 against -0.862. THE REST OF THE ATTACK AGREES. Slippage on the stop entry takes the dislocation state from -0.647 to -2.615 at two extra spreads. The parameter grid is negative at every one of twenty combinations of barrier width and exit horizon. Both eras negative, 2 of 9 and 1 of 9 markets. USDSEK -1.107 against a baseline of -1.076. FAILURE CODES: INTRABAR_AMBIGUITY, now resolved rather than assumed, and EXECUTION_UNRELIABLE. The sealed holdout remains examined: false.

entries.why: The final report named gold's unknown short-side swap as the single most decision-relevant open item, because the overnight verdict turns on it: 0.2038 spreads a night is breakeven and the known long rate is 1.2616. That framing makes the conclusion depend on an external lookup that is a per-broker, per-day snapshot I cannot verify or reproduce. There is a better move available. The corrected scaling exponent is 0.233 rather than 0.536, and at that rate the edge is so slow to grow with horizon that even ZERO financing may not reach one round trip at any horizon a person could hold. If that is so, the swap number stops mattering and the question closes on measured data instead of on a website. The ladder currently stops at one week, which is where the measurement is thinnest and where the local slope steepens to 0.504 - so the honest way to settle it is to measure further out rather than extrapolate a fit five times past its anchor, which is exactly the error the intraday file was built to catch.
entries.change: Extend the timeframe ladder past a week to two weeks, one month and one quarter by exact aggregation of the cleaned H1 bid and ask series, and measure the same previous-bar fade on each with the ratio of means and a month-block bootstrap. Then, using the MEASURED points rather than a fitted line, compute for every horizon the net after a round trip plus financing at rates from zero to the known gold long rate, find the horizon that maximises net at each rate, and solve for the financing rate at which the best horizon breaks even. Report the zero-financing case explicitly, because that is the best case any broker could offer and it bounds every other.
entries.criterion: The financing question is CLOSED if the best net over all measured horizons is negative even at a financing rate of exactly zero, since no venue can do better than free carry and the exact swap then cannot change the verdict. It remains OPEN if some horizon is positive at zero financing, in which case the break-even financing rate at that horizon is the number to compare against a real swap sheet and the lookup becomes worth doing. Either way the horizons beyond a week carry few bars - about 264 monthly and 88 quarterly per market - so any positive figure out there must be reported with its interval and treated as underpowered rather than as a finding.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 on the cleaned frame, aggregated upward. No holdout is touched.

result.note: CLOSED. Every horizon on the extended ladder is negative at a financing rate of exactly zero, and no venue can charge less than nothing, so gold's unknown short-side swap can no longer change the verdict. The lookup the final report called its most decision-relevant open item is moot. THE LADDER PAST A WEEK, WHICH IS WHAT SETTLES IT. Edge in round trips with 95% intervals: H1 +0.1203 [+0.065, +0.176] on 9 of 9; H4 +0.1099 on 8 of 9; D1 +0.1648 on 7 of 9; W1 +0.4397 [-0.774, +1.764] on 7 of 9; W2 +0.2415 on 5 of 9; M1 -2.2143 on 5 of 9; Q1 -6.5896 on 4 of 9. Best net at zero carry is -0.560 at W1. THE SHAPE REVERSES AND THAT RETRACTS MY OWN EXTRAPOLATION. The edge peaks at one week and falls after it. The fitted exponent of 0.233 was an average over a ladder that rises and then turns, so the 8,900-hour crossing quoted in the final report describes nothing real - it applied a fit far past its anchor, which is the exact error the intraday file was built to avoid, and I made it anyway in prose after avoiding it in code. THE INTERVAL DOES NOT EXCLUDE A POSITIVE NET AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. W1 has 1,071 bars a market and a net interval of [-1.774, +0.764], whose upper end is above zero. On the point estimate it fails; on the interval it is not established either way. WHAT CLOSES IT ANYWAY IS THE HORIZON ITSELF. W1 is seven nights, so carry is charged seven times. At 0.05 spreads a night - a twenty-fifth of gold's known long rate - W1 falls to -0.910 and the best horizon reverts to H1 at -0.882. The only horizon whose interval reaches positive is the one that any nonzero swap destroys fastest, and every rate above zero leaves H1 as the best at about -0.88. FAILURE CODES: COST_DOMINATED and TIMEFRAME_INAPPROPRIATE. The sealed holdout remains examined: false.
